qa-function VERIFY proof: connector walked-edge penalty fix (SweepRoute.kt), uncommitted on HEAD 931794a.
Change under test: shortestPath() gained walked: Set<Pair<Long,Long>> (default emptySet); edges whose undirected key is already in `walked` (toured earlier by the spiral) cost WALKED_EDGE_PENALTY(3.0)x their length, so mid-spiral connectors prefer fresh streets over deadheading swept ground. closeLoop's return leg calls shortestPath WITHOUT `walked` (plain shortest path home, exempt per AC-24e). ShibuyaSweepTest's AC-24b revisit bound tightened 0.20 -> 0.12.
VERDICT: PASS (see qa-function's chat response for the full numbered findings / criteria table).
Command: cd walk-sim && JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17 ./gradlew --no-build-cache clean test --console=plain
Sections: 1) GREEN: final run, fix as shipped (WALKED_EDGE_PENALTY=3.0). Full 77-test suite: 77 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 1 skipped (pre-existing, unrelated: ShibuyaFixtureBaker, env-gated live-HTTP re-bake tool). 2) RED probe: WALKED_EDGE_PENALTY temporarily set to 1.0 (neutralises the penalty: stepCost = length times 1.0 = length, byte-for-byte the pre-fix cost function) to prove the tightened 0.12 bound is a real, non-vacuous regression guard, not a bound loosely chosen to already pass. Captured, then the mutation was reverted immediately; `git diff -- walk-sim/core-sim/.../SweepRoute.kt` after revert matched the shipped fix exactly (WALKED_EDGE_PENALTY = 3.0, no probe residue), and `git status` was clean of any qa-function-authored changes before this proof was written.
